verdict: These are the same caret — same deepskyblue, same 3 CSS px width, same rounded caps, same full-line-box height — except that B's lands on the pixel grid and A's misses it by a fifth of a pixel and half a pixel vertically. That fifth of a pixel is the whole argument: A's caret has an 80%-opacity left edge, a 19%-opacity ghost column on its right, and half-lit tips, so when it blinks it fades in as a smudge rather than switching on as a blade. B's is six columns of solid ink, off or on, nothing in between. Neither app earns any credit for the caret itself: a saturated #00BFFF bar overshooting the capline by 18–20 px and hanging 16 px past the 'p' descender is the loudest object on a near-white page, and with no selection in either shot the selection colour is simply unjudgeable.

states.name: selection
states.gap: The band is the full 74px pitch carrying roughly 40px of ink (32px ascender-to-baseline plus a 9px descender) — 1.85x the ink height, so the slab of blue visually outweighs the four words inside it; A's 70px is 4px less bulk for the same #ccedf8.
states.gapTheirs: Selection band is 70px tall on a 74px line pitch (94.6%), so consecutive selected rows cannot tile — a 4px unselected f7f7f7 stripe combs through every multi-line selection; B's band is exactly 74px and tiles gapless. The band is also off-centre on the ink: 19px of blue above the ascenders vs 13px below the descenders, a 3px upward bias against B's 1.5px.
states.verdict: Neither app will show me a caret — there is no vertical bar of any width, any tone, anywhere in either frame, which for a caret-and-cursor judgement is both sides failing the actual question. Given only the selection to go on, A's band is 70px inside a 74px line: drag down three paragraphs and you get hairline gutters striping the block, the combed look that reads as a rendering bug rather than a decision. B's band is the exact line pitch and sits 1.5px off the ink centre instead of 3px, so it tiles clean and doesn't lean. That 4px is the whole of it, and it is the only thing either image gives me to decide on.
